description: Power BI is an interactive data visualization software product developed by Microsoft with a primary focus on business intelligence.
painPoints: Per-user licensing gets expensive at scale ($10/user/month)
Steep learning curve for DAX and advanced features
Limited customization compared to open-source alternatives
Requires Microsoft ecosystem for best experience

alternatives.name: Tableau
alternatives.reason: More powerful visualization capabilities, better for exploratory analysis

alternatives.name: Looker Studio
alternatives.reason: Completely free, web-based, good enough for most SMB dashboards

alternatives.name: Grafana
alternatives.reason: Free, open-source, excellent for time-series and operations dashboards

migrationGuide: Export Power BI reports as PBIX. For Tableau, rebuild dashboards (no direct import). For Looker Studio, rebuild using Google connectors. For Grafana, connect to the same data sources.
verdict: Tableau is best for enterprise BI. Looker Studio is best for free, simple dashboards. Grafana is best for time-series/operations dashboards.

faqs.question: Can I open Power BI files in Tableau?
faqs.answer: No, there is no direct import. You need to rebuild dashboards in Tableau.

faqs.question: Is Looker Studio really free?
faqs.answer: Yes, Looker Studio (formerly Google Data Studio) is completely free.

description: QuickBooks is an accounting software package developed and marketed by Intuit.
painPoints: Expensive subscription ($30-100/month depending on plan)
Limited inventory features in lower tiers
Customer support can be slow
Windows-only desktop version (Mac version limited)

alternatives.name: Xero
alternatives.reason: Better Mac support, unlimited users in all plans, more intuitive UI

alternatives.name: Wave Accounting
alternatives.reason: Completely free for accounting, ideal for small businesses and freelancers

alternatives.name: GNU Cash
alternatives.reason: Free, open-source, double-entry accounting, no subscription

migrationGuide: Export your QuickBooks data as Excel/CSV. Import into Xero (has migration tools). For Wave, export as CSV and import. For GNU Cash, import using QIF or CSV.
verdict: Xero is best for small businesses wanting better Mac support. Wave is best for freelancers wanting free accounting. GNU Cash is best for free, open-source accounting.

faqs.question: Can I migrate QuickBooks to Xero?
faqs.answer: Yes, Xero has built-in migration tools for QuickBooks data.

faqs.question: Is Wave really free?
faqs.answer: Yes, Wave's core accounting features are free. They make money on payroll and payments processing.

description: Figma is a web-based graphics editing and user interface design app. It is accessed through a web browser but also has desktop apps.
painPoints: Free tier limited to 3 Figma files and 3 FigJam files
Expensive for full features ($15/month per editor)
Internet connection required (though offline mode exists)
Adobe acquisition concerns (though Figma remains independent after deal fell through)

alternatives.name: Penpot
alternatives.reason: Free, open-source, web-based, uses SVG standards (unlike Figma's proprietary format)

alternatives.name: Lunacy
alternatives.reason: Free, opens .fig files, works offline, fast performance

alternatives.name: Sketch
alternatives.reason: One-time purchase option ($99/year), Mac-only, mature UI design tool

migrationGuide: Export Figma files as FIG. Import into Penpot (SVG-based). For Lunacy, directly open .fig files. For Sketch, rebuild designs (no direct import from Figma).
verdict: Penpot is best for free, open-source, SVG-based design. Lunacy is best for free, offline .fig editing. Sketch is best for Mac users wanting a one-time purchase.

faqs.question: Can Penpot open Figma files?
faqs.answer: Not directly. Export as SVG from Figma, then import into Penpot.

faqs.question: Is Lunacy really free?
faqs.answer: Yes, Lunacy is free for personal and commercial use. Pro version ($9/month) adds advanced features.

description: InVision is a prototyping and collaboration tool for design teams.
painPoints: Expensive ($7.95/user/month for Pro)
Performance issues with large prototypes
Limited design editing capabilities
Being displaced by Figma (which has prototyping built-in)

alternatives.name: Figma
alternatives.reason: Built-in prototyping, free tier, all-in-one design + prototype

alternatives.name: Adobe XD
alternatives.reason: One-time purchase option (part of Creative Cloud), good prototyping

alternatives.name: Balsamiq
alternatives.reason: Simpler, faster for wireframing, one-time purchase option

migrationGuide: Export InVision prototypes as PDF or images. Rebuild in Figma, Adobe XD, or Balsamiq. No direct import available.
verdict: Figma is best for all-in-one design + prototyping. Adobe XD is best for Creative Cloud users. Balsamiq is best for quick wireframing.

faqs.question: Can I import InVision prototypes into Figma?
faqs.answer: Not directly. You need to rebuild prototypes in Figma.

faqs.question: Is Balsamiq good for high-fidelity prototypes?
faqs.answer: Balsamiq is designed for low-fidelity wireframes. For high-fidelity, use Figma or Adobe XD.

description: Grammarly is an American-based technology company that provides a digital writing assistance tool.
painPoints: Free tier is very limited (basic grammar only)
Expensive premium ($12/month annual)
Privacy concerns (text sent to servers for analysis)
Not always accurate with context-specific writing

alternatives.name: LanguageTool
alternatives.reason: Free, open-source, supports more languages than Grammarly, self-hostable

alternatives.name: Hemingway Editor
alternatives.reason: One-time purchase ($19.99 desktop), focuses on clarity and readability

alternatives.name: ProWritingAid
alternatives.reason: More affordable than Grammarly, better for fiction writers

migrationGuide: No data migration needed. Install the alternative browser extension or desktop app. Grammarly doesn't store your writing history in a transferable format.
verdict: LanguageTool is best for free, open-source, multi-language support. Hemingway is best for clarity-focused writing. ProWritingAid is best for fiction writers.

faqs.question: Is LanguageTool as good as Grammarly?
faqs.answer: LanguageTool is comparable for grammar checking and supports more languages. It's also open-source and self-hostable.

faqs.question: Does Hemingway Editor check grammar?
faqs.answer: Hemingway focuses on clarity, readability, and style. It's not a comprehensive grammar checker like Grammarly.
